rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.5 and 3 report the authors' own three-year (2018-2020) field experiment in a 2.1 ha young almond orchard in Hell<U+00ED>n (Spain), with Sentinel-2 NDVI/SAVI time series, pressure-chamber stem water potential, trunk perimeter and canopy diameter measurements across five treatments in three randomized blocks.
rows.notes: The study shows that severe sustained deficit irrigation (33% ETc) produced lower NDVI/SAVI (about 13%), more negative stem water potential (23%) and smaller tree dimensions (trunk perimeter about 13-15%, canopy diameter about 0.45 m) than full irrigation, while moderate deficit (67% ETc) had no effect (Section 3.1.1, 3.2, Figs 6, 9, Tables S1-S6, Conclusion). It thus supports only the diagnostic/detection part of the passage. It does not define operational thresholds for irrigation scheduling, does not report yield, and does not test whether VI-based diagnosis prevents yield losses, which is the crop_production effect claimed. The 14% 'crop size' figure refers to tree dimensions (trunk perimeter/canopy), not yield or crop size. The authors moreover state that NDVI/SAVI showed a low correlation with stem water potential (Discussion, results not shown) and have limited ability to identify short-term water status variations, which undercuts the 'precise diagnosis' framing. Detection of deficit conditions is a precondition of the claimed effect, so upstream is set to true.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion and conclusions; supplementary tables (S1-S6) referenced but not included. Study measured vegetative/physiological responses only; no yield or irrigation-scheduling outcomes were reported.
